name: Damask
desc: An ogee (pointed-arch) net of pomegranate and palmette motifs tiled in a mirrored half-drop across the frame, woven as gilt figure on a deep ground; the pattern is fixed but the satin lives -- a broad band of gilding sheen sweeps diagonally across with a trailing shadow, so the figure catches the light and darkens again exactly the way woven damask flips figure and ground as you tilt it, rendered as gold brocade, silver on charcoal, blackwork on linen, or single-colour toile.

energy.doc: overall glow driving the sheen brightness

scale.doc: motif size -- larger, fewer, more monumental cells

speed.doc: how fast the gilding sheen sweeps across

density.doc: number of motif columns across the field

sheen.doc: strength of the travelling satin sheen and its shadow

hue.doc: gilt figure hue (44 = gold); ground is complementary

style.doc: aesthetic: gold brocade on deep ground / silver on charcoal / black figure on linen / single-colour indigo toile

seed.doc: deterministic -- re-throws ground grain and cell mirroring
